title: Finite-size reliability of homothetic quantum Otto engines
authors: Gabriella G. Damas, Clebson Cruz, Norton G. de Almeida, Gao Xianlong, G. D. de Moraes Neto
abstract: Homothetic quantum Otto engines---where all populated energy gaps are rescaled by a common factor---provide a reference model in which the quasistatic stochastic efficiency is trajectory-independent while work remains fluctuating. For arbitrary finite homothetic spectra we derive the two-point-measurement work distribution and reduce the first two work moments to endpoint energy moments. Specializing to a uniformly spaced ladder gives closed finite-$N$ expressions for the full work distribution, mean work, variance, and signal-to-width reliability. This ladder connects the qubit and oscillator limits, reveals a finite-$N$ reliability crossover, and demonstrates that the high-temperature and infinite-dimensional limits do not commute. The noncommutation reflects a bounded-versus-unbounded spectral distinction: at fixed finite $N$ the Gibbs state has a normalizable infinite-temperature limit, whereas the oscillator retains an ever-expanding thermal tail. The exact formulas are used to compare standard mean-output prescriptions with work reliability, showing that maximum mean output and maximum dimensionless reliability select different operating points. The benchmark is extended to incomplete diagonal reset and to finite-time unitary strokes described by transition matrices, with a finite-ladder protocol and a harmonic sudden-switch oscillator benchmark as controlled examples. Weak deviations from exact homothety are treated perturbatively, showing how level-dependent gap distortions reintroduce quasistatic efficiency fluctuations and modify work reliability. Together, these results separate finite-size, incomplete thermalization, finite-time, and weak spectral-distortion contributions to work unreliability in quantum Otto engines.
summary: This paper develops a detailed theoretical framework to analyze the reliability of work extraction from quantum Otto engines operating with spectrally constrained (homothetic) systems. By deriving exact formulas for work distributions and moments in the finite-size limit, it quantifies how deviations from ideal conditions—such as incomplete thermalization or spectral distortion—affect performance metrics like mean output versus statistical reliability.
main_problem: The paper investigates the finite-size reliability of work extraction from quantum heat engines, focusing on how fluctuations affect performance when energy spectra are discrete and finite.
main_result: It derives explicit formulas for the full work distribution and its moments for specific spectral structures, demonstrating that high-temperature/infinite-dimensional limits do not commute with finite-size effects.
method: The analysis utilizes the Two-Point-Measurement (TPM) construction to calculate work statistics, specializing on homothetic spectra and extending the framework to include incomplete thermalization and finite driving times.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum Otto engine operating with 'homothetic' energy gaps, meaning all populated energy gaps are rescaled by a common factor. The system can be specialized to a uniformly spaced ladder connecting qubit and oscillator limits.
key_observables: Work distribution, mean work ($\langle W angle$), variance ($\sigma^2_W$), and signal-to-width reliability ($R_N$).
important_parameters: Finite number of energy levels ($N$), the scaling factor $\alpha$, temperature parameters ($ eta_h,  eta_l$), and spectral distortion measures.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that work statistics can be accurately derived using the Two-Point-Measurement (TPM) construction for energy-diagonal endpoint states; it also assumes quasistatic operation in the adiabatic limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the finite-$N$ crossover of reliability ($R_N$) for a uniform ladder, comparing exact results to infinite limits. Other figures compare mean work and reliability under sudden switches versus adiabatic driving.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using homothetic engines, derives moment equations via TPM, specializes these derivations for the uniformly spaced ladder case, compares different operational regimes (e.g., harmonic oscillator vs. ad-hoc), and finally analyzes deviations from ideal homothety.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous diagnostic tool to quantify non-ideal effects—like finite size or incomplete thermalization—in quantum energy conversion devices, which is crucial for designing practical quantum heat engines.
